**Finding submitted: deviation (critical rule IP).**

**What I found**

- **§ 4(a) (p0017)** — Works are "the property of Company" *only* "to the extent" they were created in a period that has been invoiced and the invoice paid. There is no present assignment and no interim licence, so title fragments invoice-by-invoice and any unbilled, unpaid or disputed period leaves the work product we funded owned by RadialSpark with no rights back to us. That falls short of even the fallback (perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free licence to use, modify and sublicense deliverables).
- **§ 4(d) (p0022)** — compounds the problem by deferring our right to modify the software until payment in full or termination.
- **No Customer Data ownership statement** anywhere; our data is addressed only as Confidential Information in § 8 (p0038), which is not an ownership right.

**What is acceptable and left alone**

- § 4(b) (p0020) — Contractor retains its pre-existing tools, methodologies and know-how. Fine per the rule (Vendor keeping its own platform/background IP is expected).
- § 4(c) (p0021) — perpetual, royalty-free, sublicensable licence-back to Contractor's Information embedded in the Works. Silence on "irrevocable" is noted in the rationale only, not flagged.
- No joint ownership is created.

**Redline (validated, preferred position, precedent seed-ip)** — single minimal edit to § 4(a): Works vest by irrevocable present assignment on creation "whether or not any invoice relating to such Works has then been issued or paid," plus a sentence confirming Clear Capital retains all right, title and interest in its own data, materials and IP.
